title: Undocumented-person collectives protest near Finance Tower
organizer: Several collectives of undocumented people; exact organizations not named
threshold_50_evidence: Unproven: the opened report gives no attendance count or qualitative crowd scale.

actual_occurrence.summary: BRUZZ reports multiple collectives of undocumented people protested at Finance Tower on Friday.

start_date.summary: Article dated 6 November 2020 says action occurred Friday, 6 November.

organizer.summary: Several collectives of undocumented people; names not specified.

demand.summary: They sought support and work rights tied to work-based regularization and sent a letter to the federal asylum/migration secretary.

participants_original.summary: Opened article gives no crowd size or estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No quantitative or clear qualitative evidence establishes at least 50.

state_response.summary: Police asked protesters to remove banners and leave after about 45 minutes; no other response described.

notes: The linked article headline about approximately 200 people at Luxembourg Square was dated 12 July 2020 and is outside this month; it is not evidence for the November action. BRUZZ displayed a Belga copyright credit, but written origin remains unknown. ccode 211 is the supplied provisional planning value.
open_questions: Obtain a count or qualitative threshold evidence for this specific action.
Check for actual continuity or relation to other undocumented-worker events.
End date and protester violence unknown.

title: 60-hour climate action by relaying activists
location: Namur and Brussels (announced route; actual site occupancy by date not documented)
scope: planned and underway multi-site climate action, exact executed extent unresolved
organizer: Coalition Climat, Greenpeace Belgium and named partner organizations
participants_original: 60 people participated by relaying during a 60-hour action, according to the organizer; no simultaneous count
threshold_50_evidence: Unproven. The organizer describes 60 people relaying over 60 hours; no simultaneous gathering count is reported.

actual_occurrence.summary: Organizer follow-up published 1 December says the action had started Monday morning and was ongoing.

start_date.summary: Announcement schedules the start Monday 30 November; follow-up confirms it had started by 1 December.

location.summary: Announcement schedules an itinerary from Namur to Brussels, but follow-up does not verify actual occupancy at individual sites.

participants_original.summary: 60 activists/people take turns across 60 hours, with no simultaneous attendance count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence reports 50 present at one time; total participants across relays are not a simultaneous threshold.

demand.summary: Calls on Belgium's federal and regional governments to coordinate climate policy and adopt stronger emissions reductions.

organizer.summary: Climate Coalition, Greenpeace, BBL, Oxfam-Solidarity, Youth for Climate, unions and citizen groups named in release.

notes: Onset is 30 November; the organizer's follow-up confirms an action was underway but reports 60 relaying participants rather than simultaneous attendance. Exact locations and closure remain unverified. Le Vif page returned a technical Internal Error with no HTTP denial (see S003); no retry. This onset is owned by November; December contains only a continuation reference, not a new event.
open_questions: Find a permitted contemporaneous source establishing actual participant count at a single gathering and executed site(s).
Confirm whether the route and 2 December planned finish occurred.

title: Liège march opposing curfew and calling for solidaristic public-health measures, 17 November
location: From Place des Déportés toward Place du Marché, Liège
organizer: Collective organizers not named in the opened reports
threshold_50_evidence: The report gives about 150 participants at this march, above 50.

actual_occurrence.summary: Today in Liège reports a first similar protest happened on 17 November; an article written later repeats the action details.

start_date.summary: Article dated 25 November identifies the previous Tuesday as 17 November; its subsequent article labels this the first march.

location.summary: Place des Déportés toward Place du Marché / City Hall in Liège.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The single march had a reported attendance of about 150.

demand.summary: Opposition to local curfew and call for solidaristic public-health measures, including criticism of state measures.

state_response.summary: Police reportedly did not intervene and made no administrative arrests/fines at the gathering; fines followed later, outside immediate protest response.

notes: The two reports are from the same outlet, Today in Liège; do not count them as independent sources. The later fines are a consequence, not an MM state-response category. This is kept separate from 28 November because it is a distinct date/action. ccode 211 is provisional.
open_questions: Reviewer to assess evidence and whether no-intervention justifies no_explicit on response fields.
Check related events/continuity around the adjacent months.
End date and protester violence unknown.

title: Liège march opposing curfew and calling for solidaristic public-health measures, 28 November
location: central Liège route (reports differ on streets)
Pont Saint-Léonard per Today in Liège S006
organizer: Collective organizers not named in opened report
participants_original: About 500 (Qu4tre S008); more than 1,000 (Today in Liège S006). Keep the conflict; lower estimate governs provisional count per manual.
threshold_50_evidence: Both contemporaneous local reports place the crowd far above 50: Qu4tre reports about 500 (S008), while Today in Liège reports over 1,000 (S006). Retain discrepancy and use the lower estimate provisionally.

actual_occurrence.summary: Two contemporary regional/local outlets report the Saturday 28 November anti-curfew march in Liège.

start_date.summary: Saturday 28 November is specified in the actual-event report and anticipated in the 25 November announcement.

end_date.summary: Police contained the march after 22:15 on 28 November; reported as same-day end, though precise end time unknown.

location.summary: Both reports start at Place Saint-Lambert but list differing routes and different bridges where police stopped participants; retain both source-specific locations.

participants_original.summary: Today in Liège says over 1,000; Qu4tre says around 500. These conflicting same-event estimates are preserved; the lower estimate is provisional per manual.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both estimates independently exceed 50: one reports around 500; the other over 1,000.

demand.summary: Against the curfew and for solidaristic public-health measures; challenges to restrictive state policies.

state_response.summary: Both reports document police stopping/containing the march and administrative action. Qu4tre reports 350 administrative identifications/detentions, 17 administrative custodial arrests and three later judicial arrests; categories may overlap and are not summed.

notes: A distinct march from the 17 November action; same broader curfew campaign is not sufficient reason to merge. Reported city damage is not clearly attributed to this march; protester violence remains unknown. Fines and identity checks are documented consequences but not separate coding categories. ccode 211 is provisional. Qu4tre S008 supplies an independent same-event estimate of about 500, compared with over 1,000 in S006; retain both, apply lower-estimate guidance provisionally, and flag for review. Source routes and bridge of containment differ. Damage appears in Qu4tre but perpetrator attribution is not clear, and its report says link of a separate fire remained unresolved; protester violence stays unknown.
open_questions: Reviewer to assess differing crowd estimates, route accounts and arrest/identification categories.
Determine whether the reported route damage can be attributed to protesters; the Qu4tre account does not clearly identify perpetrators.
